chunk_text: # Access Control and Password Policy ## Purpose This SOP governs authentication, password rules, and periodic access review for all company systems. ## Password Requirements - Minimum password length: 12 characters, including at least one number and one special character. - Passwords must be rotated every 90 days. - Password reuse is blocked for the last 10 passwords. ## Account Lockout - Accounts are locked after 5 consecutive failed login attempts. - Lockout duration is 30 minutes, after which

attempts. - Lockout duration is 30 minutes, after which the account automatically unlocks. ## Multi-Factor Authentication Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all privileged and administrator accounts. Standard user accounts must enable MFA within 30 days of account creation. ## Access Review The Security Team reviews all user access rights quarterly. Any access not justified by current role requirements must be revoked within 5 business days of the review.

# Data Backup and Retention Policy ## Purpose This policy defines backup scheduling, retention, and recovery objectives for all production systems. ## Backup Schedule - Full backups run every Sunday at 02:00 IST. - Incremental backups run daily at 23:00 IST. - Backup jobs are monitored by the Infrastructure Team; any failed job must be re-run within 4 hours of the failure alert. ## Retention - Daily incremental backups are retained for 45 days. - Monthly full backup archives are retained for 1 year.

Monthly full backup archives are retained for 1 year. - Backups older than the retention window are securely purged automatically. ## Recovery Objectives - Recovery Time Objective (RTO): 4 hours. - Recovery Point Objective (RPO): 24 hours. ## Restoration Testing Backup restoration must be tested quarterly by restoring a sample dataset to a staging environment and verifying data integrity. Results are logged in the quarterly compliance report.

# Incident Response SOP ## Purpose This Standard Operating Procedure defines how the organization detects, triages, escalates, and closes out operational incidents. ## Severity Levels and Response Times - Severity 1 (Critical): must be acknowledged by the on-call engineer within 15 minutes of detection. An Incident Commander must be assigned within 30 minutes of acknowledgement. - Severity 2 (High): must be acknowledged within 1 hour of detection. - Severity 3 (Medium): must be acknowledged within

- Severity 3 (Medium): must be acknowledged within 4 business hours. - Severity 4 (Low): must be acknowledged within 2 business days. ## Incident Commander Responsibilities The Incident Commander owns the incident end-to-end: coordinating responders, communicating status to stakeholders every 30 minutes during a Severity 1 event, and declaring when the incident is resolved. ## Escalation If a Severity 1 incident is not acknowledged within the 15 minute window, it is automatically escalated to the

minute window, it is automatically escalated to the Duty Manager on-call rotation. ## Post-Incident Review A post-incident review report is due within 5 business days after an incident is closed. The report must include a root cause analysis and at least one corrective action item. ## Log Retention All incident logs, including chat transcripts and timeline entries, must be retained for 180 days from the incident closure date.

# Emergency Shutdown SOP ## Purpose Defines the procedure for an emergency shutdown of plant equipment. ## Trigger Conditions - Reactor pressure exceeds 12.5 bar. - Coolant flow drops below 40 litres per minute. ## Shutdown Sequence 1. The operator must press the Emergency Stop within 10 seconds of the alarm. 2. Isolate the feed valve within 2 minutes. 3. Notify the Shift Supervisor immediately. ## Restart Authorization Restart requires written sign-off from the Plant Safety Officer, and may not
sign-off from the Plant Safety Officer, and may not occur less than 6 hours after an emergency shutdown.
